slides.title: ODD+LLM: Specifying LLM-Agent Behavior for Reproducible Social Simulation
slides.highlight: This paper introduces ODD+LLM, a protocol extension that standardizes the documentation of LLM-agent components like prompt assembly and memory, addressing critical reproducibility gaps in social simulations where implementation details are often undefined.

card.one_liner: Proposes ODD+LLM, a documentation standard specifying LLM-agent behavior to ensure reproducible social simulations.
card.key_idea: Extends the ODD protocol with five blocks detailing prompt assembly, memory serialization, parsing, and retry logic for LLM agents.
card.evaluation: Multiverse analysis of a naming-game simulation and a review of 28 papers, showing 77% of binding/resolution items are undetermined.
card.limitation: Demonstration relies on a single case study with one model; the protocol has not yet been validated for improving actual reconstruction.

slides.title: AVCC: Audio-Visual Conversation Corpus for Turn-Taking Prediction with a Human Benchmark
slides.highlight: The AVCC corpus provides a public benchmark for multiparty next-speaker prediction using single-camera and microphone setups, directly addressing the sensor constraints relevant to HyECHO's goal of observing hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: Introduces AVCC, a single-sensor audio-visual benchmark for next-speaker prediction with human baselines.
card.key_idea: Converts AVCC into a public benchmark with speaker-disjoint test partitions, transcripts, and human reference data for turn-taking.
card.evaluation: Scored RoleVAP and MuVAP against 154 human participants on 1,730 events using balanced accuracy for hold/shift and next-speaker tasks.
card.limitation: Human participants lacked access to cues within the silence gap, potentially underestimating performance on short gaps.

slides.title: Rhythmic-Semantic Co-Speech Gestures for Emotional Dialogue in Robots
slides.highlight: This work presents a system generating both rhythmic and semantic co-speech gestures based on emotional state, validated on the Haru social robot. It aligns with RwB's focus on embodied social robots and enhancing human-robot interaction through expressive non-verbal cues.

card.one_liner: Emotion-aware system generates rhythmic and semantic co-speech gestures for robots using text-only input.
card.key_idea: Lightweight BERT/RoBERTa models predict iconic gesture timing/intensity and beat intensity from text and emotion, merging them into real-time robot motion.
card.evaluation: Trained on BEAT2; deployed on robot Haru. Online user study (N=60) showed higher speech-gesture alignment and preference over LLM/random baselines.
card.limitation: Text-only inference ignores prosody; iconic gestures rely on predefined animation libraries; evaluated only on one non-humanoid robot platform.

slides.title: Teaching the Harness: Student-Aware Skill Transfer for LLM Agents
slides.tldr: THEORY OF MIND FOR LLM TEACHING
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates how Theory of Mind principles enable a teacher LLM to build learner models and transfer skills effectively, directly supporting ADAM-CHAT's goal of AI teammates that infer partner intent and adapt at test time.

card.one_liner: Student-Aware Teaching uses Theory of Mind to create skill libraries that improve LLM agent performance by 5.4%.
card.key_idea: Teacher builds a learner model with empirical profiles and analytical hypotheses, tests them with diagnostic probes, and admits only validated skills.
card.evaluation: Claude-Sonnet-5 taught DeepSeek-V4-Flash on five task suites; SAT achieved 86.46% success, outperforming agnostic teaching and baselines.
card.limitation: Benefits require students capable of following instructions; gains vanish for very small models or near-ceiling performers.

slides.title: Dyship: Leveraging Acoustic Features For Speaker Relationship Classification From Dyadic Conversations
slides.highlight: This paper demonstrates that conventional acoustic features and self-supervised representations can effectively classify speaker familiarity and kinship in dyadic conversations, offering insights relevant to HyECHO's goal of modeling social relationships and group norms in human-AI interactions.

card.one_liner: DyShip classifies speaker relationships from dyadic audio, outperforming LLMs using acoustic features.
card.key_idea: Compares five speech representations (spectral, WavLM, x-vectors, articulatory) with ResNet/SVM classifiers for familiarity and kinship prediction.
card.evaluation: Tested on Seamless Interaction corpus; metrics include accuracy, F1, AUC; results exceed reported human and audio LLM baselines.
card.limitation: Single dataset with few test dyads, class imbalance in kinship, and lack of explicit turn-taking or temporal modeling.

slides.title: AVCORP: Identifying and Resisting Deception via Communication Theory and Theory of Mind
slides.highlight: This work introduces a corpus and training method for LLM agents to detect deception using Theory of Mind and communication theory, directly supporting ADAM-CHAT's goal of enabling AI teammates to infer partner intent and maintain alignment in human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: AVCORP corpus trains LLM detectors to identify deception in Avalon games using Theory of Mind reasoning traces.
card.key_idea: Constructs 5,000 annotated utterances linking 37 communication tactics to nested Theory of Mind reasoning traces, then fine-tunes Qwen3-8B via SFT and GRPO.
card.evaluation: Tested on held-out synthetic games and human Avalon-NLU data; trained detectors outperform untrained baselines and match frontier models like Claude Opus.
card.limitation: Relies on synthetic dialogue lacking human nuance; training uses gold prior traces, causing potential error cascades during inference.

slides.title: Xinhua launches world's first bionic humanoid robot news anchors
slides.highlight: The deployment of bionic humanoid robots as news anchors demonstrates advanced human-robot interaction and embodied presence in public-facing roles, offering insights relevant to the development of socially engaging embodied AI systems.

slides.title: A computational framework for understanding embodied plans
slides.tldr: GENEA FRAMEWORK FOR EMBODIED PLAN REASONING
slides.highlight: The GenEA framework demonstrates how generative models of action planning can enable AI to reason about human embodied goals, offering a potential architecture for social robots to interpret user intentions.

card.one_liner: GenEA, a generative model coupling biomechanics with intuitive physics, accurately predicts human reasoning about embodied plans.
card.key_idea: Extends task-and-motion planning with a dynamics level simulating intuitive physics, creating a joint distribution over goals and embodied plans.
card.evaluation: Tested on manipulation and navigation tasks with human data; outperformed TAMP, heuristics, and GPT-5 in predicting judgments and response times.
card.limitation: Relies on predefined symbolic action primitives and coarse biomechanics, potentially limiting generalization to complex, unstructured real-world environments.

slides.title: Pandemonium: Longform Target-Speaker Speech Recognition with Cross-Speaker Interactions
slides.highlight: This work introduces cross-speaker attention and longform processing to target-speaker ASR, enabling more accurate modeling of speaker interactions and group dynamics relevant to HyECHO's goal of perceiving hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: Pandemonium achieves state-of-the-art multi-talker ASR via longform Parakeet and cross-speaker attention.
card.key_idea: Integrates diarization conditioning into longform Parakeet, adding cross-speaker attention and an STNO mask refiner to model speaker interactions.
card.evaluation: Tested on NSF, AMI, ICSI, and others using cpWER; outperforms DiCoW baselines with oracle and predicted diarization.
card.limitation: Relies on pseudo-labeled YODAS2 data; CTC training incurs slight accuracy loss compared to TDT on short chunks.

slides.title: Teamknitt: Configuring, Observing and Intervening in LLM-Agent Teams through the Lens of Dynamical-Systems and Human-Team Theory
slides.tldr: LLM TEAM CONFIGURATION AND OBSERVATION FRAMEWORK
slides.highlight: This paper introduces a framework for configuring and observing LLM-agent teams using human-team theory, addressing team-level properties and interaction dynamics relevant to understanding hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: A framework for configuring, observing, and intervening in LLM-agent teams using human-team theory.
card.key_idea: Explicitly configures agent topologies and sharing policies, offering dual explanatory views and bounded human-led interventions without inferring psychological states.
card.evaluation: System description with open reference implementation; no comparative results reported, only falsifiable hypotheses and offline demonstrations.
card.limitation: No empirical validation of topology effects; emergent states like trust are declared unmeasured, limiting theoretical transfer claims.

slides.title: Perception, Not Reasoning, Limits Visual Theory of Mind
slides.highlight: This study identifies perceptual scene-state extraction, rather than belief reasoning, as the primary bottleneck for visual Theory of Mind in vision-language models, directly informing ADAM-CHAT's need for robust intent inference in visual environments.

card.one_liner: Visual Theory of Mind failures stem from perceptual bottlenecks, not reasoning deficits.
card.key_idea: Five-condition dissociation protocol varying perceptual fidelity while holding reasoning constant, quantified by Perceptual Contribution Ratio.
card.evaluation: Tested on seven VLMs across abstract 2D and naturalistic 3D datasets; ground-truth scaffolds close gaps, while automatic parsers fail.
card.limitation: Relies on ground-truth scaffolds which may not be available in real-world scenarios; automatic parsers remain ineffective.

slides.title: Off-target posterior mass: A training-free diagnostic for fine-tuning spoken language diarization probes
slides.highlight: This paper introduces Off-target Posterior Mass (OTPM), a training-free diagnostic metric to forecast performance gains in Spoken Language Diarization (SLD) fine-tuning, which is relevant to HyECHO's goal of efficient multimodal social perception.

card.one_liner: OTPM predicts spoken language diarization fine-tuning gains using unlabelled audio and pre-trained model posteriors.
card.key_idea: Computes the fraction of LID posterior mass assigned to non-target languages to forecast probe gains via linear regression.
card.evaluation: Validated on synthetic FLEURS pairs (ρ=0.56) and real corpora (SEAME, VoxPopuli, DISPLACE) using Whisper models and LDER.
card.limitation: Over-predicts gains on real-world data due to synthetic-real distribution shifts and ignores confusion between target languages.

slides.title: ReSUM: Reasoning-Driven Multi-Agent Framework for Query-Focused Summarization
slides.highlight: ReSUM addresses challenges in long-meeting query-focused summarization, such as complex speaker dynamics and sparse key information, by using a modular multi-LLM framework with a planner to coordinate retrieval and summarization agents. This approach enhances long-context robustness and faithfulness, offering a potential method for processing complex meeting transcripts relevant to social perception tasks.

card.one_liner: ReSUM uses a multi-agent framework with reasoning distillation to improve query-focused meeting summarization.
card.key_idea: Decouples tasks into planner, retriever, summarizer, and critique agents, using teacher LLM reasoning traces to fine-tune smaller models.
card.evaluation: Tested on QMSum and SQuALITY against zero-shot, RAG, and fine-tuned baselines using ROUGE, BERTScore, and human evaluation.
card.limitation: Relies on strong teacher LLMs for generating reasoning traces and incurs computational cost from iterative multi-agent coordination.

slides.title: From Counterfactual Edits to Human Narratives: LLM-Driven Interpretations for Recommender System Explanations
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates how LLMs can abstract low-level counterfactual edits into coherent natural language narratives, enhancing the interpretability of recommender systems. It is relevant to MIMIC for its application of LLM-based agent models to bridge the gap between technical model outputs and human-centered understanding in hybrid human-AI interactions.

card.one_liner: LLMs summarize counterfactual edits into natural language explanations for recommender systems.
card.key_idea: Uses LLMs to convert long interaction edit lists into concise narratives, optimized via Direct Preference Optimization.
card.evaluation: Tested on MovieLens-1M with human-calibrated metrics; DPO improved correctness and informativeness across multiple LLMs.
card.limitation: Performance depends on underlying counterfactual generator quality; large edit sets remain challenging to interpret.

slides.title: Beyond the Transcript: Measuring and Improving the Use of Acoustic Information in Audio Language Models
slides.tldr: ENHANCING ACOUSTIC UNDERSTANDING IN AUDIO LMS
slides.highlight: This work distinguishes tasks requiring acoustic analysis (e.g., speaker identity, emotion, intonation) from those solvable by transcript alone, demonstrating that targeted training can significantly improve the use of acoustic information already encoded in model layers. This is relevant to HyECHO as it addresses the core challenge of extracting non-lexical social cues like identity and engagement from audio streams.

card.one_liner: Audio LLMs underuse acoustic cues; targeted LoRA training improves attribute and structure accuracy.
card.key_idea: Identify layers where acoustic readout declines, train LoRA adapters there with a content anchor to improve paralinguistic understanding.
card.evaluation: Tested 19 open models and Gemini on 92 tasks; LoRA repair raised attribute/structure accuracy by 12-44pp while preserving lexical scores.
card.limitation: Repair validated on only two models; synthetic reading references may introduce bias; transfer to unseen formats remains uneven.

slides.title: Sage-Taiyi: A Metacognitive Architecture for Scientific Discovery
slides.highlight: Sage-Taiyi demonstrates how explicit metacognitive monitoring and control can adapt research targets and reasoning methods, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's goal of AI teammates that self-correct and infer intent for effective human-AI teaming.

card.one_liner: Sage-Taiyi uses metacognitive monitoring to guide scientific ideation, outperforming baselines on Taiyi-Bench.
card.key_idea: A two-level architecture where meta-level monitoring updates a cognitive state to regulate object-level search targets and reasoning methods.
card.evaluation: Ranked first on Taiyi-Bench (54.0 vs 47.9) and external benchmarks; validated via expert collaborations in chemistry and materials science.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: How Many Exposures Does a World Model Need? Learning Unseen Game Mechanics at Test Time
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates that world models can learn unseen game mechanics through test-time parameter updates, achieving high prediction accuracy with limited exposures. This aligns with ADAM-CHAT's goal of AI teammates that adapt at test time beyond in-context learning.

card.one_liner: World models learn unseen game mechanics in ~80 exposures via test-time training, tripling agent efficiency scores.
card.key_idea: WARC, a 35M-parameter vision transformer, performs online test-time training with gradient updates after each transition to learn environment mechanics.
card.evaluation: MechEval on ARC-AGI-3 (69 mechanics, 20 games) and closed-loop play; WARC-Agent triples explorer efficiency score (0.15 to 0.46).
card.limitation: Results limited to deterministic, discrete 64x64 grid games; untested on continuous/stochastic dynamics or goal modeling.

slides.title: Embodied AI Unveils Factory Robot That Learns from Human Workers
slides.highlight: This development highlights the growing trend of robots acquiring skills through direct human interaction, a core principle in embodied social robotics and human-robot collaboration.

slides.title: Adaptive Residual Quantization for Memory-Efficient Temporal Action Segmentation
slides.highlight: The ARQ-VAE method enables efficient storage of long-form procedural video features, which is relevant to MOSAIC's need to retain historical data for incremental human-AI coadaptation without catastrophic forgetting.

card.one_liner: Adaptive residual quantization compresses video features by allocating variable code depths per frame based on reconstruction difficulty.
card.key_idea: Trains an RQ-VAE, then adaptively truncates residual chains per frame to minimize reconstruction error, followed by decoder fine-tuning.
card.evaluation: Tested on GTEA, 50Salads, Breakfast, and YTI using MS-TCN/ASFormer; outperforms TCA/GNI in storage-performance trade-offs.
card.limitation: Requires pre-extracted features and a two-stage training process; performance depends on the initial RQ-VAE's reconstruction quality.

slides.title: A human-in-the-loop Control Paradigm for Construction Robotics: From VR-Guided Teleoperation to Semi-Autonomous Dual-Arm Operation
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates a control paradigm that dynamically adjusts human involvement based on task uncertainty, aligning with MOSAIC's goal of coadaptive human-AI interaction by balancing autonomy with shared control for resilience.

card.one_liner: A human-in-the-loop paradigm enabling structured transitions from VR teleoperation to semi-autonomous dual-arm construction.
card.key_idea: Integrates VR guidance, rule-based skill primitives, and shared-autonomy with explicit role allocation and command-priority rules.
card.evaluation: Validated on dual-arm platform for façade tasks with 10 novice operators; measured performance, robustness, and NASA-TLX workload.
card.limitation: Relies on manually defined rule-based skills and predefined weights, lacking adaptive learning for unstructured environments.

slides.title: Evaluating LLM-Generated World Models for Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates that mechanical validity of LLM-generated world models is insufficient for faithful neuro-symbolic reasoning, a critical insight for MIMIC's integration of LLM-based agent models in hybrid human-AI society simulations.

card.one_liner: Mechanically valid LLM-generated world models often lack structural fidelity, risking errors in downstream safety reasoning.
card.key_idea: Evaluates LLM-generated POSGs via mechanical validity, structural agreement, and semantic checks to test if executability implies faithfulness.
card.evaluation: Benchmark of 44 scenarios across five LLMs; 134/135 valid game models had low structural F1 (0.366), revealing significant discrepancies.
card.limitation: Small hand-crafted benchmark, discrete symbolic models, and incomplete human validation of semantic criteria limit generalizability.

slides.title: Where to Approximate in Neurosymbolic Inference?
slides.highlight: This work improves the scalability of probabilistic neurosymbolic methods by optimizing where approximation budgets are allocated in weighted model counting, using tensor train decompositions to achieve significantly more accurate inference.

card.one_liner: Tensor train approximations in neurosymbolic compilation yield orders-of-magnitude more accurate inference than fuzzy methods.
card.key_idea: Unifies compilation into a three-step pipeline, using tensor train decompositions for factor approximation and SVD-based recompression during multiplication.
card.evaluation: Tested on Sudoku, arithmetic, and scene understanding; shows superior WMC accuracy and learning performance over fuzzy and exact baselines.
card.limitation: Requires careful rank budget management; excessive recompression can degrade model fidelity despite low aggregate error.
